paras.text: One big defect in the agricultural system of Pakistan is that the division and ownership of land is extremely unequal and unjust, because most of the land is in the possession of feudal lords and landlords, whereas a large part of the rural population is itself deprived of ownership of land; rather they work or labour as tenants of landlords. sections.theory:
Causes of unemployment (Causes of Unemployment)

Unemployment in Pakistan is of two kinds: in villages unemployment is seven per cent and in cities ten per cent. Its important reasons are these:

1. Defective land system (Land Tenure System)

One big defect in the agricultural system of Pakistan is that the division and ownership of land is extremely unequal and unjust, because most of the land is in the possession of feudal lords and landlords, whereas a large part of the rural population is itself deprived of ownership of land; rather they work or labour as tenants of landlords. For this reason, because of deprivation of the basic means of livelihood, i.e. land, most of the rural population does not get employment according to need, and they are victims of unemployment. Its estimate is made thus: in Punjab one-fifth of cultivated land is owned by such big feudal lords and landlords whose number is only half a per cent (0.5) of the total owners, whereas eighty per cent of owners own only one-third of the land. In Sindh about seventy per cent of the cultivable area is owned by only seven per cent of waderas and landlords, and in the Frontier province forty-eight per cent (i.e. about half) of cultivated land is owned by khans (i.e. feudal lords). (Reference: “The grip of the feudal lords”.) (Remember that the French Revolution came in 1798, because of which the feudal system was ended in France and other countries of Europe.)

2. Shortage of small industries and handicrafts

An effective means of providing employment to the rural population is domestic and small-scale industries and handicrafts; but in our villages these industries could not flourish to a satisfactory extent. Therefore employment opportunities (Employment Opportunities) could not be created according to need, and the problem of unemployment has taken a severe form.

3. Absence of infrastructure (Low Infrastructure)

In the rural economy there is a shortage of basic facilities for economic progress and the promotion of employment, e.g. means of transport, means of news-giving, roads, markets, financial institutions, electricity, natural gas etc. Thus, because of the shortage of infrastructure, employment opportunities could not be created to the desired extent.

4. Unproductiveness of the education system

In the present education system of Pakistan, the majority is of students obtaining non-technical and arts education, and after graduating they cannot work in some technical sector or occupation; rather their productivity is low; therefore they are victims of unemployment.

5. Political disorder and economic instability (Instability)

Pakistan has not been granted political and economic peace and stability, because of which the economic progress of the country has not occurred at a smooth and satisfactory speed, nor could employment opportunities be created.

6. Over-population

The total population in Pakistan is 191.71 million individuals. Further, the rate of increase in population is 1.86%. The country’s economy is not able to provide employment to the growing population.

sections.content:
Causes of unemployment (Causes of Unemployment)

Unemployment in Pakistan is of two kinds: in villages unemployment is seven per cent and in cities ten per cent. Its important reasons are these:

1. Defective land system (Land Tenure System)

One big defect in the agricultural system of Pakistan is that the division and ownership of land is extremely unequal and unjust, because most of the land is in the possession of feudal lords and landlords, whereas a large part of the rural population is itself deprived of ownership of land; rather they work or labour as tenants of landlords. For this reason, because of deprivation of the basic means of livelihood, i.e. land, most of the rural population does not get employment according to need, and they are victims of unemployment. Its estimate is made thus: in Punjab one-fifth of cultivated land is owned by such big feudal lords and landlords whose number is only half a per cent (0.5) of the total owners, whereas eighty per cent of owners own only one-third of the land. In Sindh about seventy per cent of the cultivable area is owned by only seven per cent of waderas and landlords, and in the Frontier province forty-eight per cent (i.e. about half) of cultivated land is owned by khans (i.e. feudal lords). (Reference: “The grip of the feudal lords”.) (Remember that the French Revolution came in 1798, because of which the feudal system was ended in France and other countries of Europe.)

2. Shortage of small industries and handicrafts

An effective means of providing employment to the rural population is domestic and small-scale industries and handicrafts; but in our villages these industries could not flourish to a satisfactory extent. Therefore employment opportunities (Employment Opportunities) could not be created according to need, and the problem of unemployment has taken a severe form.

3. Absence of infrastructure (Low Infrastructure)

In the rural economy there is a shortage of basic facilities for economic progress and the promotion of employment, e.g. means of transport, means of news-giving, roads, markets, financial institutions, electricity, natural gas etc. Thus, because of the shortage of infrastructure, employment opportunities could not be created to the desired extent.

4. Unproductiveness of the education system

In the present education system of Pakistan, the majority is of students obtaining non-technical and arts education, and after graduating they cannot work in some technical sector or occupation; rather their productivity is low; therefore they are victims of unemployment.

5. Political disorder and economic instability (Instability)

Pakistan has not been granted political and economic peace and stability, because of which the economic progress of the country has not occurred at a smooth and satisfactory speed, nor could employment opportunities be created.

6. Over-population

The total population in Pakistan is 191.71 million individuals. Further, the rate of increase in population is 1.86%. The country’s economy is not able to provide employment to the growing population.

پاکستان میں بے روزگاری دو طرح کی ہے: دیہات میں بے روزگاری سات فیصد اور شہروں میں دس فیصد ہے۔ اس کی اہم وجوہات یہ ہیں:

1۔ ناقص نظامِ اراضی: (Land Tenure System)

پاکستان کے زرعی نظام میں ایک بڑا نقص یہ ہے کہ زمین کی تقسیم اور ملکیت انتہائی غیر مساویانہ اور غیر عادلانہ ہے۔ کیونکہ اراضی کا بیشتر حصہ جاگیرداروں اور زمینداروں کے قبضے میں ہے جب کہ دیہی آبادی کا کثیر حصہ خود اپنی ملکیتی اراضی سے محروم ہے، بلکہ وہ زمینداروں کے مزارع کے طور پر کام یا مزدوری کرتے ہیں۔ اس وجہ سے بنیادی ذریعہ معاش یعنی زمین سے محرومی کے باعث، دیہی آبادی کے بیشتر لوگوں کو حسبِ ضرورت روزگار نہیں ملتا اور وہ بے روزگاری کا شکار ہیں۔ اس کا اندازہ یوں ہوتا ہے کہ پنجاب میں زیرِ کاشت زمین کا پانچواں حصہ ان بڑے جاگیرداروں اور زمینداروں کی ملکیت ہے جن کی تعداد کل مالکان کا محض آدھا فیصد (0.5) ہے، جبکہ اسی فیصد مالکان کی ملکیت میں صرف ایک تہائی زمین ہے۔ سندھ میں قابلِ کاشت اراضی کا تقریباً ستر فیصد رقبہ صرف سات فیصد وڈیروں اور زمینداروں کی ملکیت ہے، اور صوبہ سرحد میں زیرِ کاشت زمین کا اڑتالیس فیصد (یعنی تقریباً نصف) حصہ خوانین (یعنی جاگیرداروں) کی ملکیت ہے۔ (حوالہ: جاگیرداروں کا شکنجہ) (یاد رہے کہ انقلابِ فرانس 1798ء میں آیا تھا جس کے باعث فرانس اور یورپ کے دیگر ملکوں میں جاگیرداری نظام ختم کر دیا گیا تھا)۔

2۔ چھوٹی صنعتوں اور دستکاریوں کی قلت:

دیہی آبادی کو روزگار دلانے کا ایک مؤثر ذریعہ گھریلو اور چھوٹے پیمانے کی صنعتیں اور دستکاریاں ہوتی ہیں، لیکن ہمارے دیہات میں یہ صنعتیں اطمینان بخش حد تک فروغ نہیں پا سکیں۔ اس لیے روزگار کے مواقع (Employment Opportunities) حسبِ ضرورت پیدا نہیں ہو سکے اور بے روزگاری کا مسئلہ شدت اختیار کر گیا ہے۔

3۔ تحتی ڈھانچے کی عدم موجودگی: (Low Infrastructure)

دیہی معیشت میں معاشی ترقی اور روزگار کے فروغ کے لیے بنیادی سہولتوں کی قلت ہے، مثلاً: ذرائع نقل و حمل، ذرائع خبر رسانی، سڑکیں، منڈیاں، مالی ادارے، بجلی، قدرتی گیس وغیرہ۔ لہٰذا تحتی ڈھانچے کی کمی کے باعث روزگار کے مواقع مطلوبہ حد تک پیدا نہیں ہو سکے۔

4۔ تعلیمی نظام کی غیر پیداواریت:

پاکستان کے موجودہ تعلیمی نظام میں غیر فنی اور آرٹس کی تعلیم حاصل کرنے والے طلبہ کی اکثریت ہے اور وہ فارغ التحصیل ہو کر کسی تکنیکی شعبے یا پیشے میں کام نہیں کر سکتے، بلکہ ان کی پیداواریت کم ہوتی ہے، اس لیے وہ بے روزگاری کا شکار ہیں۔

5۔ سیاسی بدامنی اور معاشی عدمِ استحکام: (Instability)

پاکستان کو سیاسی اور معاشی امن و استحکام نصیب نہیں ہو سکا، جس کے باعث ملک کی معاشی ترقی ہموار اور تسلی بخش رفتار سے نہیں ہوئی اور نہ روزگار کے مواقع پیدا ہو سکے۔

6۔ افراطِ آبادی:

پاکستان میں کل آبادی 191.71 ملین افراد ہے۔ نیز آبادی میں اضافہ کی شرح 1.86% ہے۔ ملکی معیشت بڑھتی ہوئی آبادی کو روزگار فراہم کرنے کے قابل نہیں ہے۔

sections.title: باب 9 — متن (22)

paras.text: 7. Shortage of technical education
paras.urdu: 7۔ فنی تعلیم کی کمی:
paras.pashto: 7. د تخنیکي زده‌کړې کمښت

paras.text: Our present education system is unable to give technical and mechanical training. Without vocational education obtaining employment is not possible.
paras.urdu: ہمارا موجودہ نظامِ تعلیم فنی اور تکنیکی تربیت دینے سے قاصر ہے۔ پیشہ ورانہ تعلیم کے بغیر روزگار کا حصول ممکن نہیں۔
paras.pashto: زموږ اوسنی تعلیمي نظام د تخنیکي او فني روزنې له ورکولو عاجز دی. له مسلکي زده‌کړې پرته د روزګار ترلاسه کول شوني نه دي.

paras.text: 8. Dependence on the agricultural sector
paras.urdu: 8۔ زرعی شعبہ پر انحصار:
paras.pashto: 8. پر کرنیزې برخې تکیه

paras.text: 43.5 per cent of Pakistan’s manpower is working in the agricultural sector. With very much dependence on the agricultural sector, it cannot provide employment to all manpower. We should use our manpower in other sectors too.
paras.urdu: پاکستان کی افرادی قوت کا 43.5 فیصد حصہ زرعی شعبہ میں کام کر رہا ہے۔ زرعی شعبہ پر بہت زیادہ انحصار تمام افرادی قوت کو روزگار فراہم نہیں کر سکتا۔ ہمیں اپنی افرادی قوت دیگر شعبوں میں بھی استعمال کرنی چاہیے۔
paras.pashto: د پاکستان د بشري ځواک ۴۳.۵ سلنه برخه په کرنیزه برخه کې کار کوي. پر کرنیزې برخې ډېره تکیه ټول بشري ځواک ته روزګار نه شي برابرولی. موږ باید خپل بشري ځواک په نورو برخو کې هم وکاروو.

paras.text: 9. Shortage of savings
paras.urdu: 9۔ بچتوں میں کمی:
paras.pashto: 9. د سپما کمښت

paras.text: Savings are very necessary for investment. In Pakistan the rate of savings is 14.5 per cent. Such low savings cannot increase investment. If there is no investment, people will remain unemployed.
paras.urdu: بچتیں سرمایہ کاری کے لیے بہت ضروری ہیں۔ پاکستان میں بچتوں کی شرح 14.5 فیصد ہے۔ اتنی کم بچتیں سرمایہ کاری کو بڑھا نہیں سکتیں۔ اگر سرمایہ کاری نہیں ہوگی تو لوگ بیروزگار رہیں گے۔
paras.pashto: سپما د پانګونې لپاره ډېره اړینه ده. په پاکستان کې د سپما نرخ ۱۴.۵ سلنه دی. دومره لږه سپما پانګونه نه شي زیاتولی. که پانګونه ونه شي، خلک به بې‌روزګاره پاتې شي.

paras.text: 10. Imbalance of the demand and supply of labour
paras.urdu: 10۔ محنت کی طلب اور رسد کا عدمِ توازن:
paras.pashto: 10. د کار د غوښتنې او عرضې عدم توازن

paras.text: In different sectors the imbalance of the demand and supply of labour becomes a cause of unemployment. In rural areas unemployment is more compared with cities.
paras.urdu: مختلف شعبوں میں محنت کی طلب اور رسد کا عدمِ توازن بیروزگاری کا باعث بنتا ہے۔ دیہاتی علاقوں میں بیروزگاری شہروں کی نسبت زیادہ ہے۔
paras.pashto: په بېلابېلو برخو کې د کار د غوښتنې او عرضې عدم توازن د بې‌روزګارۍ لامل ګرځي. په کلیوالو سیمو کې بې‌روزګاري د ښارونو په پرتله ډېره ده.

paras.text: 11. Political instability
paras.urdu: 11۔ سیاسی عدمِ استحکام:
paras.pashto: 11. سیاسي بې‌ثباتي

paras.text: Since independence the country has not attained correct political stability. One after another, governments kept changing quickly, and the country has remained a victim of poor governance (Poor Governance); therefore long-term and solid-based plans for economic progress could not be made. In 1954 the constituent assembly was dissolved. In 1958 the late Ayub Khan enforced martial law in the country. In September 1965 war took place with India. At the end of 1968 country-wide disturbances took place against former President Ayub Khan; in March 1969 President Yahya Khan enforced martial law in the country. In 1970, because of the national elections, conditions remained uncertain; during 1971 Sheikh Mujib-ur-Rahman’s six points became a cause of calamity. In 1971 war broke out with India and the country broke into two parts. From 1972 the period of the Peoples Party government began; banks, insurance companies and many industrial institutions were taken into national custody, because of which severe discouragement occurred to the private business sector and production became less. After the March 1977 election a country-wide movement went on until, on 5 July 1977, overturning the Bhutto government, General Zia enforced martial law in the country.
paras.urdu: آزادی کے بعد اب تک ملک کو صحیح سیاسی استحکام نصیب نہیں ہو سکا۔ یکے بعد دیگرے جلد جلد حکومتیں بدلتی رہیں، اور ملک ناقص حکمرانی (Poor Governance) کا شکار رہا ہے، اس لیے معاشی ترقی کے لیے طویل المیعاد اور ٹھوس بنیادوں پر منصوبے نہیں بنائے جا سکے۔ 1954ء میں دستور ساز اسمبلی توڑ دی گئی۔ 1958ء میں مرحوم ایوب خان نے ملک میں مارشل لاء نافذ کر دیا۔ ستمبر 1965ء میں بھارت سے جنگ ہوئی۔ 1968ء کے آخر میں سابق صدر ایوب خان کے خلاف ملک گیر ہنگامے ہوئے، مارچ 1969ء میں صدر یحییٰ خان نے ملک میں مارشل لاء نافذ کر دیا، 1970ء میں قومی الیکشنوں کے باعث حالات مخدوش رہے، 1971ء کے دوران شیخ مجیب الرحمٰن کے چھے نکات مصیبت کا باعث بنے رہے، 1971ء میں بھارت سے جنگ لگ گئی اور ملک دو حصوں میں ٹوٹ گیا۔ 1972ء سے پیپلز پارٹی کا دورِ حکومت شروع ہوا، بنک، بیمہ کمپنیاں اور بہت سے صنعتی ادارے قومی تحویل میں لے لیے گئے، جس کے باعث نجی کاروباری شعبہ کی سخت حوصلہ شکنی ہوئی اور پیداوار کم ہو گئی۔ مارچ 1977ء کے الیکشن کے بعد ملک گیر تحریک چلی تا آنکہ 5 جولائی 1977ء کو بھٹو حکومت کا تختہ الٹ کر جنرل ضیا نے ملک میں مارشل لاء نافذ کر دیا۔
paras.pashto: له خپلواکۍ وروسته تر اوسه هېواد ته سم سیاسي ثبات نصیب شوی نه دی. یو په بل پسې حکومتونه ژر ژر بدل شول، او هېواد د بدې حکمرانۍ (Poor Governance) ښکار پاتې شو؛ نو د اقتصادي پرمختګ لپاره اوږدمهاله او پر کلکو بنسټونو پلانونه جوړ نه شول. په ۱۹۵۴ کې اساسي قانون جوړوونکې اسمبلۍ منحله شوه. په ۱۹۵۸ کې مرحوم ایوب خان په هېواد کې مارشل لا پلي کړ. د ۱۹۶۵ په سپتمبر کې له هندوستان سره جګړه وشوه. د ۱۹۶۸ په پای کې د پخواني ولسمشر ایوب خان پر ضد په ټول هېواد کې ګډوډۍ وشوې؛ د ۱۹۶۹ په مارچ کې ولسمشر یحیی خان مارشل لا پلي کړ. په ۱۹۷۰ کې د ملي ټاکنو له امله حالات ناڅرګند پاتې شول؛ د ۱۹۷۱ په ترڅ کې د شیخ مجیب الرحمن شپږ ټکي د مصیبت لامل وو. په ۱۹۷۱ کې له هندوستان سره جګړه ونښته او هېواد په دوو برخو ووېشل شو. له ۱۹۷۲ څخه د پیپلز ګوند د حکومت دوره پیل شوه؛ بانکونه، د بیمې شرکتونه او ډېرې صنعتي ادارې ملي تحویل ته واخیستل شوې، چې له امله یې خصوصي سوداګریزه برخه سخته نا هڅول شوه او تولید لږ شو. د ۱۹۷۷ د مارچ له ټاکنو وروسته په ټول هېواد کې غورځنګ روان شو، تر دې چې د ۱۹۷۷ د جولای په ۵ مه جنرال ضیا د بوټو حکومت نسکور کړ او مارشل لا یې پلي کړ.

paras.text: In August 1988, after the death of the late President Zia, elections were held on a party basis for the national and provincial assemblies, in which the Peoples Party made its government in the centre and in the provinces of Sarhad and Sindh, whereas in Punjab and Balochistan the parties opposing the Peoples Party established governments. Because of this disagreement severe obstruction fell on political stability and economic development.
paras.urdu: اگست 1988ء میں صدر ضیا مرحوم کے انتقال کے بعد جماعتی بنیادوں پر قومی اور صوبائی اسمبلیوں کے لیے الیکشن ہوئے، جس میں پیپلز پارٹی نے مرکز اور صوبہ سرحد و سندھ میں اپنی حکومت بنائی جب کہ پنجاب اور بلوچستان میں پیپلز پارٹی کی مخالفت جماعتوں نے حکومتیں قائم کیں۔ اس اختلاف کے باعث سیاسی استحکام اور معاشی ترقی میں سخت رکاوٹ پڑی۔
paras.pashto: د ۱۹۸۸ په اګست کې د مرحوم ولسمشر ضیا له مړینې وروسته د ملي او ولایتي اسمبلیو لپاره پر ګوندي بنسټ ټاکنې وشوې، چې په کې پیپلز ګوند په مرکز او د سرحد او سند په ولایتونو کې خپل حکومت جوړ کړ، حال دا چې په پنجاب او بلوچستان کې د پیپلز ګوند مخالفو ګوندونو حکومتونه جوړ کړل. د دې اختلاف له امله په سیاسي ثبات او اقتصادي پرمختګ کې سخت خنډ پېښ شو.

paras.text: On 6 August 1990 President Ghulam Ishaq Khan ended the Peoples Party’s Benazir government and dissolved the national and provincial assemblies, because of which economic conditions again became a victim of stagnation. In October 1990 fresh elections were held, as a result of which the Peoples Party was defeated and the Islami Jamhoori Ittehad formed the government.
paras.urdu: چھ اگست 1990ء کو صدر غلام اسحاق خان نے پیپلز پارٹی کی بے نظیر حکومت ختم کر دی اور قومی و صوبائی اسمبلیاں توڑ دیں، جس کے باعث معاشی حالات پھر تعطل کا شکار ہو گئے۔ اکتوبر 1990ء میں از سرِ نو الیکشن ہوئے جن کے نتیجہ میں پیپلز پارٹی کو شکست ہوئی اور اسلامی جمہوری اتحاد نے حکومت تشکیل دی۔
paras.pashto: د ۱۹۹۰ د اګست په ۶ مه ولسمشر غلام اسحاق خان د پیپلز ګوند د بې‌نظیر حکومت پای ته ورساوه او ملي او ولایتي اسمبلۍ یې منحلې کړې، چې له امله یې اقتصادي حالات بیا د ځنډ ښکار شول. د ۱۹۹۰ په اکتوبر کې بیا ټاکنې وشوې چې په پایله کې یې پیپلز ګوند ماتې وخوړه او اسلامي جمهوري اتحاد حکومت جوړ کړ.

paras.text: In April 1993, once again, the President of Pakistan (for the third time in five years) dissolved the National Assembly and dismissed the cabinet. In June it was restored by the decision of the Supreme Court, but because of the mutual confrontation and conflict of the President (Ghulam Ishaq Khan) and the Prime Minister (Nawaz Sharif) the Prime Minister had to resign. 7. Shortage of technical education

Our present education system is unable to give technical and mechanical training. Without vocational education obtaining employment is not possible.

8. Dependence on the agricultural sector

43.5 per cent of Pakistan’s manpower is working in the agricultural sector. With very much dependence on the agricultural sector, it cannot provide employment to all manpower. We should use our manpower in other sectors too.

9. Shortage of savings

Savings are very necessary for investment. In Pakistan the rate of savings is 14.5 per cent. Such low savings cannot increase investment. If there is no investment, people will remain unemployed.

10. Imbalance of the demand and supply of labour

In different sectors the imbalance of the demand and supply of labour becomes a cause of unemployment. In rural areas unemployment is more compared with cities.

11. Political instability

Since independence the country has not attained correct political stability. One after another, governments kept changing quickly, and the country has remained a victim of poor governance (Poor Governance); therefore long-term and solid-based plans for economic progress could not be made. In 1954 the constituent assembly was dissolved. In 1958 the late Ayub Khan enforced martial law in the country. In September 1965 war took place with India. At the end of 1968 country-wide disturbances took place against former President Ayub Khan; in March 1969 President Yahya Khan enforced martial law in the country. In 1970, because of the national elections, conditions remained uncertain; during 1971 Sheikh Mujib-ur-Rahman’s six points became a cause of calamity. In 1971 war broke out with India and the country broke into two parts. From 1972 the period of the Peoples Party government began; banks, insurance companies and many industrial institutions were taken into national custody, because of which severe discouragement occurred to the private business sector and production became less. After the March 1977 election a country-wide movement went on until, on 5 July 1977, overturning the Bhutto government, General Zia enforced martial law in the country.

In August 1988, after the death of the late President Zia, elections were held on a party basis for the national and provincial assemblies, in which the Peoples Party made its government in the centre and in the provinces of Sarhad and Sindh, whereas in Punjab and Balochistan the parties opposing the Peoples Party established governments. Because of this disagreement severe obstruction fell on political stability and economic development.

On 6 August 1990 President Ghulam Ishaq Khan ended the Peoples Party’s Benazir government and dissolved the national and provincial assemblies, because of which economic conditions again became a victim of stagnation. In October 1990 fresh elections were held, as a result of which the Peoples Party was defeated and the Islami Jamhoori Ittehad formed the government.

In April 1993, once again, the President of Pakistan (for the third time in five years) dissolved the National Assembly and dismissed the cabinet. In June it was restored by the decision of the Supreme Court, but because of the mutual confrontation and conflict of the President (Ghulam Ishaq Khan) and the Prime Minister (Nawaz Sharif) the Prime Minister had to resign. Then on 6 and 9 October 1993 elections were held for the national and provincial assemblies, and in October 1993 for the third time the Peoples Party’s (Benazir) government came into power, in whose period in Karachi between the government and the (political party) MQM … (continued on p.184)

7. Shortage of technical education

Our present education system is unable to give technical and mechanical training. Without vocational education obtaining employment is not possible.

8. Dependence on the agricultural sector

43.5 per cent of Pakistan’s manpower is working in the agricultural sector. With very much dependence on the agricultural sector, it cannot provide employment to all manpower. We should use our manpower in other sectors too.

9. Shortage of savings

Savings are very necessary for investment. In Pakistan the rate of savings is 14.5 per cent. Such low savings cannot increase investment. If there is no investment, people will remain unemployed.

10. Imbalance of the demand and supply of labour

In different sectors the imbalance of the demand and supply of labour becomes a cause of unemployment. In rural areas unemployment is more compared with cities.

11. Political instability

Since independence the country has not attained correct political stability. One after another, governments kept changing quickly, and the country has remained a victim of poor governance (Poor Governance); therefore long-term and solid-based plans for economic progress could not be made. In 1954 the constituent assembly was dissolved. In 1958 the late Ayub Khan enforced martial law in the country. In September 1965 war took place with India. At the end of 1968 country-wide disturbances took place against former President Ayub Khan; in March 1969 President Yahya Khan enforced martial law in the country. In 1970, because of the national elections, conditions remained uncertain; during 1971 Sheikh Mujib-ur-Rahman’s six points became a cause of calamity. In 1971 war broke out with India and the country broke into two parts. From 1972 the period of the Peoples Party government began; banks, insurance companies and many industrial institutions were taken into national custody, because of which severe discouragement occurred to the private business sector and production became less. After the March 1977 election a country-wide movement went on until, on 5 July 1977, overturning the Bhutto government, General Zia enforced martial law in the country.

In August 1988, after the death of the late President Zia, elections were held on a party basis for the national and provincial assemblies, in which the Peoples Party made its government in the centre and in the provinces of Sarhad and Sindh, whereas in Punjab and Balochistan the parties opposing the Peoples Party established governments. Because of this disagreement severe obstruction fell on political stability and economic development.

On 6 August 1990 President Ghulam Ishaq Khan ended the Peoples Party’s Benazir government and dissolved the national and provincial assemblies, because of which economic conditions again became a victim of stagnation. In October 1990 fresh elections were held, as a result of which the Peoples Party was defeated and the Islami Jamhoori Ittehad formed the government.

In April 1993, once again, the President of Pakistan (for the third time in five years) dissolved the National Assembly and dismissed the cabinet. In June it was restored by the decision of the Supreme Court, but because of the mutual confrontation and conflict of the President (Ghulam Ishaq Khan) and the Prime Minister (Nawaz Sharif) the Prime Minister had to resign.
